page.description: Android-x86 editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: The Android-x86 project's port of Android Pie to ordinary PC hardware, shipped as live-and-installable ISO images for 64-bit and legacy 32-bit machines.
pros: Runs Android apps on a PC without a virtual machine.
Boots live from the stick before anything is installed.
The 64-bit image supports UEFI and Secure Boot.
Two architectures: modern 64-bit PCs and older 32-bit BIOS machines.
cons: The 9.0 line is unmaintained: no security fixes since 2020.
Android on a desktop needs workarounds for Play services and drivers.
No 32-bit UEFI, so very old tablets stay out.
No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed, so this page is logo-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for Android-x86; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Write the ISO to a USB stick and boot it live, or use the installer on the stick to install to a disk or partition; the installer's automatic option erases the whole disk.

editions.name: Standard (64-bit)
editions.description: The 64-bit Android 9 image on the 4.19 LTS kernel, for most modern PCs.
editions.usbNote: 921 MB image. Write it with dd or any image writer; writing erases the stick.

editions.name: Legacy (32-bit)
editions.description: The 32-bit image for older machines with a legacy BIOS.
editions.usbNote: 726 MB image. Write it with dd or any image writer; writing erases the stick.
